title: The Sovereign's Terms
summary: The Riftgate is not a door. It is a negotiation that has been in progress for thirty years. The Sovereign has been waiting for the party — not this party specifically, but a party sufficient to the conversation. The ending depends on what the party has become.

phases.label: Force or find a way through the Riftgate's outer defenses

onComplete.text: The outer defenses were designed to stop an army, not a party that has been moving for two acts. Inside, the architecture is wrong — built for something with different spatial assumptions than humans. The Sovereign's presence is not metaphorical. It is architectural.

phases.label: Navigate the Architect's Verge to reach the Sovereign's approach

onComplete.text: The Verge was built before the Ashen Veil. Before the Brightfall Council. Before the compact. Whatever the Architects were doing here, they were doing it with the full knowledge of what the Rift is and what it wants. There are warnings in eleven languages. The twelfth language does not have a name in any record the party has found.

phases.label: Cross Ember Hollow — the Sovereign's corrupted approach

onComplete.text: Ember Hollow was a community once. Forty-six years ago. The collapse was described as a geological event in the Brightfall Council records. The bodies in the right positions for a geological event. The buildings are not.

phases.label: Reach the Sovereign's chamber at the Rift's edge

onComplete.text: The chamber is not what was expected. The Sovereign is not a monster. It is a person — or was, or is becoming something that was a person once and retains the grammar of personhood without all of its content. It speaks. It has been speaking. It has been waiting for someone to hear it correctly.

phases.label: Confront the Emberveil Sovereign — fight, parley, or witness ascension

onComplete.text: The Sovereign is resolved. The Rift remains — but its relationship to the world has changed in some way that will take years to understand.

phases.label: Seal the Rift, collapse it, or leave it open — and get out

onComplete.text: The Riftgate is behind them. Whatever the Ember Rift becomes from here is something the world will have to live with. The party has done what parties do: they made it through. What follows is not a party problem. It is an era problem.
